## **GitHub repo:** <https://github.com/Tepavich/EC422_PS2_Tepavich.git>

### Data

```{r}
## Data: monthly unemployment rate data from the US, Oregon, California, Texas, and New York since 1976 from FRED
library(tidyverse)
unemp_raw <- read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")
head(unemp_raw)
```

### Wrangling

```{r}
## Wrangling:
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace(
      unemployment_rate,
      date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

unemp_recent <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= "2015-01-01")

unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_top_increases <- slice_max(unemp, unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)
unemp_top_decreases <- slice_min(unemp, unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)

unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- slice_max(
  filter(unemp, lubridate::year(date) != 2020), unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid  <- slice_min(
  filter(unemp, lubridate::year(date) != 2020), unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)

library(knitr)

kable(unemp_summary, col.names = c("region", "mean rate", "min rate", "max rate"), caption = "Unemployment Rate Summary")
kable(unemp_recent_summary, col.names = c("region", "mean rate", "min rate", "max rate"), caption = "Unemployment Rate Summary Since January 2015")
kable(unemp_top_increases_no_covid, caption = "Top Increases in the Unemployment rate excluding 2020")
kable(unemp_top_decreases_no_covid, caption = "Top Decreases in the Unemployment rate excluding 2020")
```

### Visualization

```{r}
## Visualization:
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rates by Region", x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rates by Region", x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = fct_reorder(region, mean_rate), y = mean_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Mean Unemployment Rate by Region", x = "Region", 
       y = "Mean Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(
  bind_rows(unemp_top_increases_no_covid, unemp_top_decreases_no_covid), aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate_change, color = region)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Top Increases and Decreases in Unemployment Rate", x = "Date", 
       y = "Change in Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
#I plotted the top increases and decreases in the unemployment rate excluding Covid. 
#I was curious to see which regions in which years were the most extreme changes in the unemployment rate.
```

### Reflection

Most of the code was pretty straight forward to follow. There were a couple times that I got error messages and I had to do some trouble shooting with AI to figure out what I was doing wrong. I am definitely more comfortable with some of the basic mechanics of R such as piping as well as just some general formatting things.
